# Steps `dev/ci_contract.py` permits to name a tool, and the reason each does.
#
# An entry is `workflow.yml:Step name`. Every line is a debt with an owner, not
# a dispensation: the file exists so the unconverted surface is a number
# someone can burn down instead of a silence.

# --- runner-plane -----------------------------------------------------------
# Acts on the MACHINE, not the product. `bootstrap.sh` lives on the dev runner
# and provisions a worktree there; it has no local meaning.
bootstrap-branch.yml:Validate issue dispatch
bootstrap-branch.yml:Bootstrap local worktree

# --- CI-plane bookkeeping ---------------------------------------------------
# Project-board automation: reads and writes GitHub state through `gh`, which
# is already permitted, and differs only in reaching it through a shell
# conditional.
add-to-project.yml:Set target date to created_at + 30 days

# --- pending ----------------------------------------------------------------
# Installs the provider CLIs the prerequisite gates spawn, UNPINNED and
# globally: `npm install -g @openai/codex @anthropic-ai/claude-code`. Two
# unpinned global installs decide what a gate is testing. Recipe needed:
# `init-tools` should provision them, which is what that phase is for.
test.yml:Install the provider CLIs these gates require

# Three `alembic` invocations that walk a migration to head, back to base, and
# to head again. A real gate with no recipe, so nobody can run it before
# pushing a migration. Recipe needed: `test-migrations`.
migrations.yml:Exercise migration round trip

# --- pending, the release lane ----------------------------------------------
# This repository's product IS the frozen onedir, and release.yml is the only
# thing that has ever produced one. Nothing below can be run by a developer,
# which is why a break in it surfaces at release with the tag already cut.
# It is also the fleet's worst single offender: `Prove the frozen tree is one
# the consumer can install` is a 75-line Python program embedded in YAML.
#
# Recipes needed, in the order they would retire these entries:
#   build-binary            the freeze itself; vaultspec-dashboard's
#                           a2a-product-contract.yml reaches into this
#                           repository and runs scripts/build_binary.py
#                           directly, so a recipe is the only stable contract
#                           between the two repos
#   check-frozen-tree       the 75-line heredoc, moved into dev/ where it can
#                           be tested and run
#   test-artifact-lifecycle prove_artifact_lifecycle.sh is bash, and the
#                           Windows leg runs it under Git Bash - the exact
#                           platform assumption a recipe removes
#   build-archive           the tar/7z branch and its sha256 sidecar
#   check-tag-version       vaultspec-core asserts the same thing about its own
#                           tag with its own copy
#   check-release-cohort    the four-target completeness check, which lists the
#                           targets by hand in a second place
release.yml:Install Python
release.yml:Resolve a host Python for the release scripts
release.yml:Resolve and agree the version
release.yml:Refuse to freeze for an architecture this runner is not
release.yml:Install the locked freeze environment
release.yml:Freeze the runtime
release.yml:Prove the frozen tree is one the consumer can install
release.yml:Prove the artifact starts, serves, and stops
release.yml:Archive the onedir
release.yml:Refuse an incomplete cohort
release.yml:Upload the assets to the release
